cti:
Threat report (sample) - Healthcare sector, Europe

Ransomware operators target hospitals and clinic groups. Initial access is gained through spearphishing with attachments (macros, ISO/LNK) or by exploiting unpatched exposed VPNs/firewalls. Attackers use valid accounts bought from initial access brokers.
After access: PowerShell execution, Cobalt Strike deployment, LSASS dumping (Mimikatz), Kerberoasting, lateral movement via RDP and PsExec/SMB, EDR tampering and shadow copy deletion (vssadmin), exfiltration to cloud storage (Rclone/MEGA) before encrypting ESXi servers and file shares.
In addition, state-sponsored espionage campaigns target medical research: software supply chain compromise, web shells on exposed Exchange servers, persistence through scheduled tasks and slow exfiltration over HTTPS.

scenarios.name: Ransomware via spearphishing with a malicious attachment
scenarios.actors: Ransomware operators targeting the healthcare sector
scenarios.summary: Initial compromise through a phishing email carrying a macro document or an ISO/LNK file, followed by payload loading, credential theft, lateral movement and encryption of hospital servers and shares.
scenarios.rationale: Vector explicitly observed against European hospitals. Critical impact on the availability of patient records and care activities.

scenarios.name: Exploitation of an exposed VPN or firewall leading to ransomware
scenarios.summary: Exploitation of an unpatched exposed appliance to gain initial access, deploy Cobalt Strike, spread across the domain and encrypt the infrastructure.
scenarios.rationale: Exposed appliances are cited as a frequent vector. Hospitals often have many critical remote access points.

scenarios.name: Use of valid accounts bought from Initial Access Brokers
scenarios.summary: Logon with already compromised accounts, environment discovery, privilege escalation and preparation of a double-extortion attack.
scenarios.rationale: The report explicitly mentions purchased accounts. Privileged identities quickly give access to hospital information systems.

scenarios.name: Double extortion with exfiltration to cloud storage
scenarios.summary: Collection of patient records and sensitive data before encryption, with exfiltration through cloud services such as Rclone or MEGA.
scenarios.rationale: Patient records are a high-value target and carry a high regulatory risk in a hospital context.

scenarios.name: Encryption of ESXi hypervisors
scenarios.summary: After compromising the environment, attackers target ESXi servers to disrupt virtualised clinical services at scale.
scenarios.rationale: ESXi assets are explicitly mentioned in the client profile and in the threat report. Maximum operational impact.

scenarios.name: Exposed Exchange compromise with a web shell
scenarios.summary: Exploitation of an exposed Exchange server, web shell deployment, collection of strategic information then stealthy exfiltration.
scenarios.rationale: The report specifically mentions this modus operandi in espionage campaigns targeting medical research.

scenarios.name: Medical research espionage through the software supply chain
scenarios.summary: Introduction of a compromised software component into the hospital environment to keep long-term access and exfiltrate research data.
scenarios.rationale: Less likely than ransomware but relevant for organisations involved in research or clinical trials.

scenarios.name: Stealthy persistence through scheduled tasks and slow HTTPS exfiltration
scenarios.summary: Long-term access over several months through scheduled tasks and gradual data extraction over HTTPS to avoid detection.
scenarios.rationale: TTP explicitly described. High confidentiality risk but more limited operational impact than ransomware.

scenarios.name: Lateral movement with PsExec and SMB from a compromised workstation
scenarios.summary: After the initial compromise of a user workstation, fast spread to the servers and network shares of the hospital domain.
scenarios.rationale: Very common in ransomware intrusions and highly dependent on internal segmentation.

scenarios.name: AD credential theft through LSASS and Kerberoasting
scenarios.summary: Acquisition of privileged credentials through LSASS and Kerberos tickets to compromise the hospital domain.
scenarios.rationale: Recurring step in the described campaigns. Useful detection to break the attack chain before the final impact.

scenarios.name: Disabling security tools before impact
scenarios.summary: Neutralising the EDR and removing traces to increase the chances of successful encryption and exfiltration.
scenarios.rationale: Activity usually observed at an advanced stage. High detection value but less discriminating as a standalone scenario.

rules.body:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001
logsource: {product: windows, category: process_creation}
detection:
  selection: {Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe', CommandLine|contains: ['-enc ', '-EncodedCommand']}
  condition: selection
rules.name: Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command
rules.note: Techniques read from the rule tags (no AI).

rules.body:
title: LSASS Memory Access by Non-System Process
tags:
  - attack.credential-access
  - attack.t1003.001
logsource: {product: windows, category: process_access}
detection:
  selection: {TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe', GrantedAccess|contains: ['0x1010', '0x1410']}
  condition: selection
rules.name: LSASS Memory Access by Non-System Process
rules.note: Techniques read from the rule tags (no AI).

rules.body:
title: Shadow Copies Deletion via Vssadmin
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1490
logsource: {product: windows, category: process_creation}
detection:
  selection: {Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe', CommandLine|contains|all: ['delete', 'shadows']}
  condition: selection
rules.name: Shadow Copies Deletion via Vssadmin
rules.note: Techniques read from the rule tags (no AI).

rules.body:
title: PsExec Service Installation
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1569.002
logsource: {product: windows, service: system}
detection:
  selection: {EventID: 7045, ServiceName: 'PSEXESVC'}
  condition: selection
rules.name: PsExec Service Installation
rules.note: PsExec-specific detection; does not by itself prove a tool transfer (T1570).

why.g4seqvc: detects the installation of the PsExec service used for remote execution over SMB.

rules.body:
title: Office Application Spawning Script Interpreter
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource: {product: windows, category: process_creation}
detection:
  selection: {ParentImage|endswith: ['\winword.exe', '\excel.exe'], Image|endswith: ['\cmd.exe', '\powershell.exe', '\wscript.exe']}
  condition: selection
rules.name: Office Application Spawning Script Interpreter
rules.note: The Office → script interpreter parent relationship indicates execution from an Office document but does not precisely distinguish macro, DDE or other mechanisms.

why.vkkwclf: detects a command interpreter launched from an Office application after user interaction.
why.g4seqvc: detects the initial malicious execution step coming from an Office document.

rules.name: Rclone Execution with Remote Config
rules.note: Rclone copy/sync strongly suggests cloud exfiltration but does not confirm the transferred content.

why.2xe2f60: detects a potential data transfer to a cloud storage service via Rclone.
why.fkcufn8: detects the exfiltration to cloud storage used in double extortion.

rules.name: Kerberoasting - Multiple TGS Requests with RC4
rules.note: Multiple RC4 TGS requests are a robust Kerberoasting indicator.

why.vkkwclf: detects a volume of RC4 TGS requests consistent with Kerberoasting activity.
why.r7235f5: directly detects the Kerberoasting step that collects service tickets.
